A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 32-page versions of SOLAR, including Appendices A–M. Text and visual inspection support reliable comparison of the methods, equations, tables, figures, and appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original SOLAR retrieval results in Table 1, ablations in Tables 2–3, and further evaluations, case studies, and timing results in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains the original retrieval experiments, ablations, and empirical appendix analyses reported in v1.

M1.justification: The architecture, two-stage training procedure, masking and segmentation components, losses, and inference pipeline remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions retain LAION-5B training, the sym-MM2MM benchmark, RefCOCO and HalDec-Bench evaluations, and the MBEIR tasks in Appendices H–I. No evaluated dataset or task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same ten supervised baselines and CLIP-SF-ZS. Appendix comparisons, including SAM and the VLM trained on mmE5's synthesized data, also retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: The 800,000 training pairs, 214 benchmark triplets, one-million-pair LAION candidate pool, evaluation metrics, training schedules, and appendix evaluation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity analyses, retrieval case studies, transformation robustness checks, and semantic-intersection analyses in Section 5 and the appendices.

E5.justification: Appendix L retains 10,000 bootstrap resamples of 214 triplets and the same 95% confidence interval, [82.9, 90.0], for SOLAR-B+D's Precision. No uncertainty-reporting or repeated-run information changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout. For example, Table 1 reports the same Avg. scores of 87.69 for SOLAR-C, 86.53 for SOLAR-B+D, and 80.61 for mmE5; all appendix results are retained.

T1.justification: The task formulation, loss equations, Gaussian assumptions, and QDA threshold derivation in Appendix C.1 are identical. Equation repositioning reflects text reflow rather than revised mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions and performance claims: symmetric MM2MM retrieval, two-stage self-supervision, a human-verified benchmark, and the reported 7.08-point advantage over mmE5.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, symmetric-versus-asymmetric task tradeoffs, and limitations are unchanged. Appendix M retains the restrictions of deletion-based sample construction and the benchmark's dependence on manual annotation.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the future-release promise with stated availability of code, model, and benchmark at the codefuse-ai/SOLAR GitHub repository. Appendix B's existing anonymous benchmark link remains. Implementation details are unchanged; repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, related-work discussion, and positioning against supervised multimodal retrieval methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract's resource-access sentence is revised, a dagger is added beside Hang Yu's name, and the arXiv version/date marking changes. The remaining prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The front-page edits produce small spacing changes and text/equation reflow across pages 1–7. Figures, tables, and captions retain their content and structure; pages 8–32 render identically.

improvement.justification: V2 provides clearer resource-access information by replacing the abstract's future-release promise with a public repository address covering code, model, and benchmark. The gain is limited because v1 already included an anonymous benchmark link and the scientific content is unchanged. Actual repository completeness cannot be established from the PDFs.
